questions.q: What two things does Mara's Python automation check, that together produce its count?
options: Group membership only, run twice for confirmation
Group membership in OT-SCADA-Admins/ot-scada-admins AND direct, individually-assigned Entra ID roles or AWS IAM policies
Only direct IAM policy attachments, ignoring groups entirely
Firewall logs from the OT/SCADA segment's network boundary
questions.explain: The automation was built to check both group membership and direct, individually-assigned access -- exactly the second data source the audit's method never looked at.

questions.q: What count does the automation report for the OT/SCADA segment as of the same October 12 cutoff the audit used?
options: 14 accounts, matching the audit exactly
9 accounts
19 accounts -- 14 via group membership and 5 via direct assignment
25 accounts
questions.explain: The automation reports 19 total: the same 14 group-based accounts the audit found, plus 5 more found only through direct, individual role or policy assignment.

questions.q: Which Azure and AWS mechanisms does the automation use to find direct, individually-assigned access?
options: Microsoft Graph appRoleAssignments/directory role endpoints, and aws iam list-attached-user-policies / list-attached-role-policies
Azure Cost Management and AWS Billing
Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts only
Azure AD sign-in logs exclusively
questions.explain: On the Azure side, Graph's appRoleAssignments and directory role assignment endpoints surface direct role grants; on the AWS side, list-attached-user-policies and list-attached-role-policies surface policies attached straight to an account rather than through a group.

questions.q: What is Mara's first move when she sees the automation's number doesn't match the audit's?
options: She assumes the audit is wrong because the automation checks more sources
She assumes the automation over-counted because the audit is the official report
She treats neither number as "wrong" yet, since a discrepancy only proves one method is measuring something the other isn't -- which requires comparing the underlying accounts to resolve
She discards both numbers and restarts the audit from scratch
questions.explain: A discrepancy between two measurements of the same thing proves only that they're measuring different inputs -- it doesn't by itself say which input is the problem, which is exactly why Mara moves to comparing underlying accounts rather than picking a number to trust by default.

questions.q: Why does it matter that the automation ran on its own existing schedule, rather than being built in response to the audit?
options: It doesn't matter at all to the story
It means the automation's higher count can't be dismissed as a tool built specifically to contradict the audit -- the coincidence of the same date makes the difference impossible to wave away
It proves the automation is less reliable because it wasn't built for this purpose
It means the automation's data is older than the audit's
questions.explain: Because the automation was already running independently of the audit and happened to measure the same access on the same day, the discrepancy can't be explained away as two tools looking at two different points in time or two different purposes.
